contract_plain_english: In the integral conservation-law setting, finite volume methods divide the domain into grid cells and approximate each cell's average state, defined as the integral of q over that cell divided by its volume. At each time step these approximate averages are modified through cell-edge fluxes. Numerical flux functions approximate the correct fluxes using the approximate cell averages as the available data [raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2, first paragraph]. The referenced continuous balance relates the time derivative of an interval's integral to its left endpoint flux minus its right endpoint flux [raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, equation (1.10)]. The selected paragraph does not specify a discrete recurrence or a quantitative accuracy guarantee [raw PDF page 27, printed page 5, Section 1.2, first paragraph].
